grades.quote: This section describes a simple paged virtual-memory system for SXLEN=64, which supports 39-bit virtual address spaces.
grades.reason: Establishes Sv39’s address width, but does not describe its address fields or their correspondence to walk.

grades.quote: walk (1497) mimics the RISC-V paging hardware as it looks up the PTE for a virtual address (see Figure 3.2). walk descends the page table tree one level at a time, using each level’s 9 bits of virtual address to index into the relevant page directory page.
grades.reason: Directly explains the correspondence between walk’s traversal levels and the 9-bit virtual-address fields used for page-table indexing.
Describes Sv32 and general paging design, not Sv39’s fields or xv6’s walk-loop indexing.
Explains safe copying through user-address translation, but provides no walk-loop levels or Sv39 address-field correspondence.
